mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant above 5.25% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to persistent higher real borrowing costs compressing equity discounting.
failure_condition: In the specified trigger regime, the 20-day forward return is non-negative in at least 60% of instances, or the 5-year rolling IC of FEDFUNDS vs. SPX is positive (>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a labor market strengthening that boosts investor confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 2% month-over-month while UNRATE falls by at least 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: In >70% of similar labor-market tightening events, the 60-day forward return is not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in retail sales (HOUST) of at least 3% for three consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as it reflects resilient consumer demand and upward earnings revisions.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by ≥3% month-over-month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: During the specified trigger, the 20-day forward return is negative in more than half of instances, or IC < -0.05 over a 12-month window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 5% in a month is associated with a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return as it signals weakening aggregate supply capacity and potential earnings compression.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >5% in a single month
failure_condition: In >80% of INDPRO contraction episodes of >5%, the 5-day forward return is non-negative (t-test p > 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly rises by more than 0.3% in a month, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to immediate market anticipation of future rate hikes.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by >0.3% in a month (unexpected)
failure_condition: In >50% of such CPI surprises, the 20-day forward return is positive or the IC of CPI vs. SPX is negative (< -0.03).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of declining labor turnover (PAYEMS falling for four consecutive months) predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as it suggests labor market stability and reduced uncertainty.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases for four consecutive months
failure_condition: During such episodes, the 60-day forward return is negative in more than 40% of cases, or the 12-month IC of PAYEMS decline vs. SPX is negative (< -0.04).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both unemployment (UNRATE) and industrial production (INDPRO) by at least 0.2 percentage points and 2%, respectively, indicates dual softening in labor and supply, which together produce a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases by ≥0.2% and INDPRO decreases by ≥2% in the same month
failure_condition: In >70% of such interaction events, the 20-day forward return is non-negative, or the IC of the combined signal vs. SPX exceeds 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent monetary easing (FEDFUNDS < 1.00%), the S&P 500 60-day forward return is expected to be positive due to lower real financing costs and increased risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: regime: FEDFUNDS < 1.00% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: In the specified regime, the 60-day forward return is negative in more than 50% of windows, or the 12-month IC of FEDFUNDS vs. SPX is negative (< -0.06).
